business_goal: let logged-in users browse the available items/products in one place so they can see what's in stock before deciding what to look into further — this is a browsing/catalog view, not a management tool.
scope: Displaying a list of sample items with basic details (name, description, price, quantity, category).
Handling loading and error states for the item listing.

functional_requirements.description: Only authenticated (logged-in) users can access the Item Listing page; an unauthenticated user is redirected to the login page.
The page displays a list of items, each showing its name, description, price, quantity, and category.
The database is pre-seeded with at least 8-10 sample items so the page has real content to show immediately, with no manual data entry needed first.
If there are no items, the page shows a clear empty state ('No items found').
While items are loading, the page shows a loading indicator; if the fetch fails, it shows a clear error message instead of a blank page.
A link to the Item Listing page is added to the site's main navigation so a logged-in user can reach it.
The system must separate product catalog data from inventory data to prevent overselling and ensure accurate stock levels.
The system must use stock movement logs instead of silent quantity updates to track changes in inventory accurately.
The system must display product availability clearly to customers, indicating whether an item is in stock or out of stock.

non_functional_requirements.description: The listing should load within a couple of seconds for a small catalog (under a few hundred items) — no pagination needed at this scale.

user_stories.goal: Browse the available items/products in one place to see what's in stock before deciding what to look into further.
user_stories.benefit: Logged-in users can easily view and assess the available products, aiding their decision-making process.

ui_expectations: A clean grid or table layout consistent with the rest of the app's existing styling.
Responsive on both desktop and mobile widths.
api_expectations: GET /api/items — returns the list of sample items.
data_requirements: Items table: id (PK), name (string), description (text), price (decimal), quantity (integer), category (string), createdAt (date).
constraints: The system must use atomic database operations to ensure data consistency and prevent race conditions.
